1. What is the direction of vibration when the particle $P$ starts to vibrate?
2. After how much time does the particle $P$ reach the wave crest for the second time?

The direction of vibration is downward.
1.9s

The wave speed arrow v points to the right, indicating that the wave propagates along the positive x direction. The visible disturbed part starts near the origin and ends at the position marked Q, whose x-coordinate is labeled 0.24 m. The curve goes upward from the equilibrium position to form a crest, then passes through the equilibrium position and goes downward to form a trough, and finally returns to the equilibrium position at Q; therefore, from the origin to Q, one complete wavelength is shown. At Q, the curve rises to the right from the trough on the left to the equilibrium line, so the spatial slope at the wavefront is positive. Point P is farther to the right, and the problem gives x_P = 0.96 m. Reasoning: From the image, read one wavelength λ = 0.24 m. The wave continues to propagate rightward from Q to P, with distance 0.96 - 0.24 = 0.72 m, so the time when P starts to vibrate is t_arrival = 0.72 / 0.6 = 1.2 s. For a wave propagating along the +x direction, there is ∂y/∂t = -v ∂y/∂x, so the direction of the particle vibration velocity is opposite to the sign of the spatial slope of the waveform. The wavefront slope at Q is positive, so when the wave reaches P, the initial vibration direction of P is the negative y direction, that is, downward. The period T = λ / v = 0.24 / 0.6 = 0.4 s. When P starts to vibrate, it is at the equilibrium position and moving downward; from this phase to the first arrival at the crest requires 3T/4, and to the second arrival at the crest requires 3T/4 + T = 7T/4 = 0.7 s. The total time relative to the start of timing is 1.2 + 0.7 = 1.9 s.

The front corresponds to phase 2π at x = Q when t = 0; particle P is not yet disturbed until the same front phase reaches it. From the text, x_P = 0.96 m and v = 0.6 m/s, so the front arrival time is (0.96 - 0.24)/0.6 = 1.2 s. The transverse velocity is ∂y/∂t = -ωA cos[k(x - vt)]; at arrival the phase is 2π, so ∂y/∂t < 0 and the initial vibration direction is downward. For crests at P, impose y = A, i.e. sin[k(x_P - vt)] = 1. After arrival, the first such phase is k(x_P - vt) = π/2, giving t = (0.96 - 0.06)/0.6 = 1.5 s. 推理：按图像建立 t=0 时刻的波形为 y=A sin(kx)，从 x=0 到 Q=0.24 m 完成一个完整周期，所以波长 λ=0.24 m，k=2π/λ。右行波可写为 y=A sin[k(x-vt)]。波前在 t=0 时位于 Q，即相位为 2π 的点在 x=0.24 m。P 点开始振动的时刻是这个波前到达 P 的时刻：t_arr=(0.96-0.24)/0.6=1.2 s。此时 P 点相位为 2π，横向振动速度 ∂y/∂t=-ωA cos[k(x-vt)]，代入 cos(2π)=1，得 ∂y/∂t<0，所以 P 开始振动时方向向下。

求 P 第二次到达波峰：波峰满足 sin[k(x_P-vt)]=1。P 开始振动后第一次波峰对应相位 π/2，因此 k(x_P-vt)=π/2，即 x_P-vt=λ/4=0.06 m，所以 t=(0.96-0.06)/0.6=1.5 s。周期 T=λ/v=0.24/0.6=0.4 s。第二次到达波峰比第一次晚一个周期，因此 t=1.5+0.4=1.9 s。
solver_metadata.model_answer:
1. Particle P starts vibrating downward.
2. Particle P reaches the wave crest for the second time after 1.9 s.

raw_record.original_question:
A transverse harmonic wave is propagating along the positive $x$-axis and has just reached point $Q$ (with a horizontal coordinate of $0.24m$). The wave speed is $v=0.6m/s$. The horizontal coordinate of particle $P$ is $x=0.96m$. Timing begins at the moment shown in the diagram.

1. What is the direction of vibration when the particle $P$ starts to vibrate?
2. After how much time does the particle $P$ reach the wave crest for the second time?
raw_record.answer:
The direction of vibration is downward.
1.9s
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure shows the instantaneous shape of a transverse wave in the x-y coordinates, and the wave speed arrow v points to the right, indicating that the wave propagates along the positive x direction. The visible disturbed part starts near the origin and ends at the position labeled Q, and the abscissa of Q is labeled as 0.24 m. The curve rises upward from the equilibrium position to form a crest, then passes through the equilibrium position and goes downward to form a trough, and finally returns to the equilibrium position at Q; therefore, from the origin to Q, one complete wavelength is shown. At Q, the curve rises to the right from the trough on the left side to the equilibrium line, so the spatial slope at the wavefront is positive. Point P is farther to the right, and the problem gives x_P = 0.96 m.

Reasoning: From the image, one reads one wavelength λ = 0.24 m. The wave continues to propagate rightward from Q to P, with a distance of 0.96 - 0.24 = 0.72 m, so the time when P begins to vibrate is t_arrival = 0.72 / 0.6 = 1.2 s. For a wave propagating along the +x direction, ∂y/∂t = -v ∂y/∂x, so the direction of the particle vibration velocity is opposite to the sign of the spatial slope of the waveform. The wavefront slope at Q is positive, so when the wave reaches P, the initial vibration direction of P is the negative y direction, namely downward. The period T = λ / v = 0.24 / 0.6 = 0.4 s. When P begins to vibrate, it is at the equilibrium position and moving downward; from this phase to the first arrival at the crest requires 3T/4, and to the second arrival at the crest requires 3T/4 + T = 7T/4 = 0.7 s. The total time relative to the start of timing is 1.2 + 0.7 = 1.9 s.
